raw_response:
Aiyo, my fields. Same six mu my father left me, I've worked them twenty-five years. Don't need no book to tell me how. Wheat in winter, maize in summer — that's the way, that's how everyone around here does it.

The wheat is in the ground already, planted last October. Soon as it warms up proper, I spread urea — about half a bag per mu, that's twenty kilos. If the color looks off, maybe a bit more. Neighbor Zhang, he always puts more than me, his yield's a little higher but he spends more too. I stick with what I know. I don't waste.

Irrigate the wheat twice usually — once late winter if dry, once at jointing when the stalk comes up. If the spring rain comes good, maybe skip one. The well's got a meter now, costs forty yuan a mu each time. Adds up quick on six mu. Before harvest I walk and look for aphids — if I see yellow bugs on the heads I spray, just a bit of stuff, fifteen twenty yuan worth. Then the hired combine comes, sixty a mu, done in a few hours. Expect four hundred, maybe four-twenty kilos a mu — that's what I got last year, year before about the same.

Then quick, right after wheat comes off in June — no time to rest. Three, four days later the seeder man comes. Fifty yuan a mu, he drills in the maize seed with the fertilizer, one bag of compound per mu. Hybrid seed, costs thirty a mu, one little sack covers my field. Middle of summer when the maize is waist-high, I side-dress urea, about twenty-five kilos a mu. That's the one that matters — maize is hungry. Irrigate once after planting if dry, maybe again at tasseling. Spray once for the corn borer — saw bad damage three years back on Old Liu's field, scared me enough I never skip.

Harvest the maize by hand — me, my wife, my son if he comes back from the city. Takes about a week. Expect four-fifty, five hundred kilos if the rain comes right.

Not much changes year to year. No reason to change what works.
